title: fix(models): preserve account reasoning effort limits
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A live account can report a narrower set of reasoning levels than the hosted model catalog. Catalog enrichment overwrote that account list, so the effort picker offered unsupported levels. This caused the [main real-Gateway UI test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44024086924/job/133840776161) to fail.

## User Impact

The picker and model consumers retain the account's reported reasoning levels, including an explicitly empty list. Hosted context limits, input capabilities, and pricing still apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registry keeps the reported effort list when describing a live-listed model with catalog metadata. When catalog compatibility is absent, it also retains the other discovered compatibility fields. This fixes the overwrite introduced by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200403 at its owner; no UI assertions or production UI code change.

## Evidence

- The existing registry test now covers missing, narrow, and empty account effort lists, plus absent catalog compatibility. The narrow and empty cases fail on the base and pass with the fix.
- 72 tests passed across the registry consumers and prompt-prefix stability suites. Targeted agents/sessions typecheck, lint, format, and diff checks passed.
- The original desktop scenario passed unchanged against a freshly built isolated Gateway and synthetic provider fixture. The picker reports `medium,ultra`, default index `0`, and the queued-request checks pass. No external provider requests were made.
- Local autoreview of the final two-file candidate against `d0daf88ab13f` was scoped-clean through P2; an independent boundary review's missing-compat finding was fixed and covered before the final review.

The runtime build passed. The lab's full declaration build remains unavailable because an existing dependency link escapes its checkout; no dependency configuration was changed. PR CI supplies broader validation.
